tests.name: Open race reasoning
tests.description: Explain the conceptual two-increment unsynchronized counter and direct run versus start.
tests.expected: Two reads of 0 followed by two writes of 1 lose one update; serial read/write pairs yield 2. No unique schedule is promised, and join alone does not protect the increment.

reasoning: The three fixed batches contain seven tokens: glow twice, ink twice and lumen three times. Every synchronized record call performs one indivisible map update on the same counter object.

Every worker is joined before snapshot. Completion and visibility after joins combine with synchronized atomic updates to justify the final counts; the result does not require any particular worker order.
Calling run directly executes on the calling thread. start creates a separate execution thread. Waiting with join does not stop two unsynchronized increments from interleaving.

For the conceptual two-increment integer race, read0/read0/write1/write1 yields 1; read0/write1/read1/write2 yields 2. This open self-check asks for possible interleavings, not one promised schedule or a fake numerical grade.

For the supplied ArrayList-backed file batches, the maximum indexed outer and inner array sizes imply a total below Long.MAX_VALUE; different collection sources need their own bound or checked arithmetic. An already-interrupted coordinator throws before starting workers; interruption while joining propagates instead of returning an incomplete snapshot. Threads are a learning mechanism here, not a speed claim or a production thread-pool design.
